To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bioelectric impedance can be used in the elderly for the measurement of whole-body and regional body composition and that the use of impedance of body segments is an alternative method for the measurement of body composition that may have advantages for some elderly patients.

(a) bioelectric impedance is an important tool for the assessment of fluid and body composition in the elderly, (b) the reference data for anthropometric measurements in the elderly are limited and require updating to include the present generations of the elderly, and (c) the bioelectric and anthropometric measurements are useful tools for the assessment of nutritional status in the elderly.
bioelectric impedance is a valid and useful method for estimating body composition in the elderly, but that reference data are needed for the present generations.

the study of the effects of the aging process on the body's water content and distribution.
the development and application of bioelectric and anthropometric techniques to assess the nutritional status of older people and to determine reference data for this population.

we have developed a new method for the assessment of total body composition in elderly persons and have shown that this method can be used to assess changes in body composition in elderly subjects over time.
the elderly, especially the very old, have a high risk of developing fluid imbalances, and this risk is increased by the presence of diseases and medications.

we can use the impedance of the body to determine the amount of fat, muscle, and water in a patient.
